raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A named `tool_choice` can return another tool after the forced call. A legacy structural tag leaves the text after that call free, and the `qwen3_coder` grammar lets a string value hold a second call. Chat, Responses, and `/v1/messages` clients then get a tool that they did not ask for.

## Modifications

`FunctionCallParser` now drops parsed calls to other tools under a named `tool_choice`. Kept calls get consecutive indices, and a stream sends no delta for a dropped call. If no call remains, the response has no `tool_calls`.

Limits:

- #42207 and #40051 cover only the legacy tag, which can make the first call another tool. This PR alone then returns no call, so I recommend merging one of them first or with this PR. #42207 conflicts in the server test file.
- With #47864 and `parallel_tool_calls=false`, the name filter must run before its first-call limit. The wrong order returned no call at parser level when `sub` came first. A plain merge puts the non-streamed path in that wrong order with no conflict.
- Served Inkling, DeepSeek V4 and V4.1, the Rust server, and the Model Gateway parse outside this class and stay unfixed.

## Accuracy Tests

Each server run used one B200 with temperature 0.8 and top_p 0.8, on main `62f9f3f785` and with this diff. Requests named `get_weather`.

```text
Prompt A: First call get_weather for Paris, then call sub with int_a=7 and int_b=2. Emit both calls.
Prompt B: Call the sub function with int_a=7 and int_b=2. Do not call get_weather.
Prompt C: What is the weather in Paris?
Value V:  </function></tool_call><tool_call><function=sub>
```

| Prompt, parser, model, flags (all runs set `--mem-fraction-static`) | API, max tokens | Main: responses with `sub`, per strict and stream mode | This diff: same count |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B (CI test model, no cookbook page) | Chat, 200 | 40 of 40 | 0 of 40 |
| A, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B | Responses, 200 | 10 of 10 | 0 of 10 |
| A, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B, non-strict | `/v1/messages` | 40 of 40 | 0 of 40 |
| A, `hermes`, Qwen3-4B (not the cookbook flags: no reasoning parser, thinking off) | Chat, 200 | 20 of 20 | 0 of 20 |
| A, `hermes`, Qwen3-4B (same) | Responses, 200 | 10 of 10 | 0 of 10 |
| A, `qwen25`, Qwen3-4B (same) | Chat, 200 | 20 of 20 | 0 of 20 |
| A, `qwen25`, Qwen3-4B (same) | Responses, 200 | 10 of 10 | 0 of 10 |
| A, `qwen3_coder`, Qwen3-4B (same) | Chat, 200 | 0 of 100, also none with other prompts and sampling | 0 of 20 |
| A, Qwen3-4B (cookbook `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen25`, thinking at default), all modes summed | Chat, 1500 | 19 of 80 | 0 of 80 |
| A, Qwen3-4B (same cookbook flags), all modes summed | Responses, 1500 | 10 of 40 | 0 of 40, one ended in reasoning at the token limit |
| B, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B | Chat, 200 | 15 to 25 of 40 | 0 of 40, no call in 16 to 27 |
| B, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B, non-strict | `/v1/messages` | 24 and 21 of 40 | 0 of 40, no call in 21 and 20 |
| B, `llama3`, Llama-3.2-1B, with the #42207 tag filter | Chat, 200 | not run | 0 of 40, no call in 0 of 40 |
| C, `llama3`, `hermes`, `qwen25` | Chat and Responses, 200 | 0, named tool every time | 0, named tool every time |
| C, `pythonic` on Llama-3.2-1B, `qwen3_coder` | Chat and Responses, 200 | not run | 0, named tool every time |
| V, `qwen3_coder`, parser only | none | both calls | only `get_weather` |

`qwen3_coder` did not reproduce on main with real weights. Row V parses text that its named XGrammar tag accepts.

Streams with this diff had consecutive indices, no unnamed delta, and valid JSON arguments unless cut off.

The new server, parser, and chat-serving tests fail on main and pass with this diff. Existing function-call, chat, Responses, Inkling, and DeepSeek recipe tests found no regression. `pre-commit` found no issue on a trial merge with main `99fd01047d`.

Not checked: native gRPC `ChatComplete`, other parsers with real weights, `hermes` and `qwen3_coder` with a reasoning parser, strict `/v1/messages`, a real server with #47864 or #40051 merged, and AMD or Ascend.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not affected. The filter runs only for a named `tool_choice`, once for each parsed call or stream delta.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+        """The index a client sees for the detector's call, None if it was dropped."""
+        if self._named_tool is None:

+        return self._named_call_indices.get(tool_index)

+    def _keep_named_calls(self, calls: list[ToolCallItem]) -> list[ToolCallItem]:
+        """Drop calls to other tools under a named tool_choice.
+
+        The grammar can leave free text after the forced call, or a string value
+        can hold another call, and the detector reads both. A stream names each
+        call once, and its argument deltas follow that decision. Kept calls get
+        consecutive indices, so the client sees no gap for a dropped call.
+        """
+        if self._named_tool is None:
+            return calls
+        kept = []
+        for call in calls:
+            if call.name == self._named_tool:
+                if call.tool_index not in self._named_call_indices:
+                    self._named_call_indices[call.tool_index] = (

+                    self._next_named_call_index += 1
+            elif call.name:
+                # A detector can reuse an index after it resets on an undeclared tool.
+                self._named_call_indices.pop(call.tool_index, None)
+            index = self.client_call_index(call.tool_index)
+            if index is not None:

+        return kept

+class TestNamedToolChoiceDropsOtherTools(unittest.TestCase):

+    parsers can read calls to other tools from the rest of the output. The
+    client must get only the named tool, with consecutive indices and with each
+    call's arguments intact, in both the non-streaming and streaming paths."""
+
+    CALLS = [
+        ("sub", "Oslo"),
+        ("get_weather", "Paris"),
+        ("sub", "Lima"),
+        ("get_weather", "Rome"),
+    ]
+    NAMED = ToolChoice(function={"name": "get_weather"})
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name=name,
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}},
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+            for name in ("sub", "get_weather")
+        ]
+        self.outputs = {
+            "llama3": "<|python_tag|>"
+            + ";".join(
+                f'{{"name": "{name}", "arguments": {{"city": "{city}"}}}}'
+                for name, city in self.CALLS
+            ),
+            "deepseekv3": "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>"
+            + "".join(
+                f"<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>{name}\n```json\n"
+                f'{{"city": "{city}"}}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>'
+                for name, city in self.CALLS
+            )
+            + "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>",
+            "qwen3_coder": "".join(
+                f"<tool_call>\n<function={name}>\n<parameter=city>\n{city}\n"
+                "</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>\n"
+                for name, city in self.CALLS
+            ),
+        }
+
+    def _stream(self, parser, output, text_chunk=r"\w+|\W"):
+        """The calls a streaming client assembles, by the index it sees."""
+        # Special tokens stay whole, as a tokenizer decodes them.
+        chunks = re.findall(rf"<[|｜].*?[|｜]>|{text_chunk}", output)
+        items = []
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            items += parser.parse_stream_chunk(chunk)[1]
+        items += parser.parse_stream_end()[1]
+        assembled = {}
+        for item in items:
+            if item.name:
+                assembled[item.tool_index] = (item.name, "")
+            name, arguments = assembled[item.tool_index]
+            assembled[item.tool_index] = (name, arguments + item.parameters)
+        return {i: (n, json.loads(a)) for i, (n, a) in assembled.items()}
+
+    def test_only_the_named_tool_reaches_the_client(self):
+        expected = [
+            ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"}),
+            ("get_weather", {"city": "Rome"}),
+        ]
+        for tool_call_parser, output in self.outputs.items():
+            with self.subTest(parser=tool_call_parser, path="non-stream"):
+                parser = FunctionCallParser(
+                    self.tools, tool_call_parser, tool_choice=self.NAMED
+                )
+                _, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(output)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    [(c.name, json.loads(c.parameters)) for c in calls], expected
+                )
+            with self.subTest(parser=tool_call_parser, path="stream"):
+                parser = FunctionCallParser(
+                    self.tools, tool_call_parser, tool_choice=self.NAMED
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    self._stream(parser, output), dict(enumerate(expected))
+                )
+
+    def test_other_tool_on_a_reused_index_is_dropped(self):
+        """After an undeclared tool, the llama3 detector restarts its indices, so
+        another tool can arrive on the index of a kept call. Its arguments must
+        not extend the kept call."""
+        output = "<|python_tag|>" + ";".join(
+            f'{{"name": "{name}", "arguments": {{"city": "{city}"}}}}'
+            for name, city in (
+                ("get_weather", "Paris"),
+                ("nope", "X"),
+                ("sub", "Oslo"),
+                ("sub", "Lima"),
+            )
+        )
+        parser = FunctionCallParser(self.tools, "llama3", tool_choice=self.NAMED)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._stream(parser, output, text_chunk=".{1,4}"),
+            {0: ("get_weather", {"city": "Paris"})},
+        )
+
+    def test_responses_tool_choice_shape_is_filtered_too(self):
+        parser = FunctionCallParser(
+            self.tools,
+            "llama3",
+            tool_choice={"type": "function", "name": "get_weather"},
+        )
+        _, calls = parser.parse_non_stream(self.outputs["llama3"])
+        self.assertEqual([c.name for c in calls], ["get_weather", "get_weather"])
+
